newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends up on expected export deals.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends up on expected export deals.

text.p: The won closed firmer versus the dollar on Tuesday as banks unloaded their dollar holdings in preparation for export negotiations expected at the end of this month, dealers said.
The won finished at 887.50 against Monday's closing of 888.20. It traded in a range of 887.50 to 888.10. The won opened at the low end of the range.

Dealers said worries of a central bank dollar-buying intervention forced participants to be cautious in dollar sales. "The dollar's decline would stop when the next support is found," said one local dealer.
The 888 won level has played the support role for more than a week until it was broken this morning.
Traders said the won was expected to move in a range of 887.00 to 887.70 on Wednesday with a base mid-rate at 887.70. Today's mid-rate was pegged at 888.30.
